title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pages 525-527): Grothendieck wants to make explicit the action of his group Γ_Q~ on SL(2,Z)^. Γ_Q~ is defined by pairs (α, β) satisfying the 'équation des lacets' (12), αρ(α)^{-1} = βσ(β)^{-1} ℓ_1^ν; it is a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group. SL(2,Z)^ is the profinite completion of π_1 of the modular stack M_{1,1}. The previous page gives a cartesian square (10): SL(2,Z)^ is the fibre product of 𝔖_{0,3}^{+∧} ≅ SL(2,Z)^/±1 (this is PSL(2,Z)^, π_1 of the j-line orbifold [P^1−{0,1,∞}/S_3]) with SL(2,Ẑ) over PSL(2,Ẑ). On PSL(2,Z)^, u = (α,β) acts on the generators of order 3 and 2 by (13): u(ρ) = int(α)ρ and u(σ) = int(β)σ. The aim is to lift this action to SL(2,Z)^, where ρ has order 6 and σ has order 4.

This page:
(14)-(15) On the congruence quotient SL(2,Ẑ), u acts by conjugation by ũ = i_{T_0}(μ) = diag(μ,1) ∈ GL(2,Ẑ). Here μ = χ(u) ∈ Ẑ^* is the multiplier (cyclotomic character). This is just the Galois action on the Tate module, whose determinant is χ.
(16) In GL(2,Ẑ) this conjugation sends ρ to ξ̲ρ and σ to η̲σ. Here ξ̲ = α̲ρα̲^{-1} and η̲ = ε β̲σβ̲^{-1}, and underlined letters denote images in GL(2,Ẑ).
(17) ε = ε_2(μ) = ±1, with ε = 1 iff μ ≡ 1 mod 4. This is the character χ_4 of Q(i)/Q.
The text then identifies ±1 with the centre of SL(2,Z)^ and writes −g = (−1)g.
(18)-(19) Lifted formulae in SL(2,Z)^: u(ρ) = int(α̃)(ρ) = ξρ and u(σ) = ε·int(β̃)(σ) = ησ. Here α̃ and β̃ are arbitrary lifts of α and β, defined up to sign. The next page notes that ξ and η are nonetheless unambiguous, and that u(ε_0) = ε_0^μ.
The next page then pushes everything to any quotient G of SL(2,Z)^. There ρ^6 = σ^4 = 1 and ρ^3 = σ^2 is a canonical central involution '−1'.

Meaning: the lift of a GT/Galois-type automorphism from PSL(2,Z)^ to the central extension SL(2,Z)^ = π_1(M_{1,1}) requires a sign twist on the order-4 generator only. That sign is the mod-4 cyclotomic character, reflecting the Galois action on the μ_4 inertia at j = 1728. No sign is needed for ρ, because −ρ has order 3 and cannot be confused with a conjugate of ρ.
errors: No genuine error found; the sign analysis checks out.

Why ε is needed for σ: σ and σ^{-1} = −σ are not conjugate in SL(2,Z_2), since norms of Z_2[i]^* are ≡ 1 mod 4. So conjugation by an SL-lift β̃ cannot produce σ^μ when μ ≡ 3 mod 4, and the factor ε = χ_4(μ) is required.

Why no sign is needed for ρ: −ρ has order 3, not 6, so conjugation alone suffices. The case μ ≡ −1 mod 3, where ρ ↦ conjugate of ρ^{-1}, is consistent only because α is allowed outside Π̂_{0,3}. The previous page writes α ∈ Π{0,τ_∞}·Π̂_{0,3}, i.e. with a transposition allowed, so int(α) can realise ρ ↦ ρ^{-1}.
Minor ambiguity: in (16) ε is written inside η̲ while (18)-(19) put it in front of int(β̃). These are equivalent since ε is central.
On the next page, 'à signe près, mod(α̃)' means the lifts are defined only modulo ±1.

ideas.what: Lifting the GT/Galois outer action from PSL(2,Z)^ (orbifold π_1 of [P^1−{0,1,∞}/S_3]) to SL(2,Z)^ = π̂_1(M_{1,1}) via the cartesian square with SL(2,Ẑ) → PSL(2,Ẑ)
ideas.modern_name: GT action on Γ̂_{1,1} / B̂_3 modulo centre; Galois action on π_1 of the moduli stack of elliptic curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld/Ihara (GT on B̂_3), Nakamura, Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps, Nakamura–Schneps (genus one), Hain–Matsumoto
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the role of M_{1,1} and SL(2,Z)^ in the tower; explicit formulae unsure

ideas.what: Congruence action given by conjugation by diag(μ,1) ∈ GL(2,Ẑ), μ = cyclotomic character
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the Tate module / monodromy compatibility

ideas.what: Sign twist ε = ε_2(μ) = χ_4(μ) on the order-4 generator σ when lifting from PSL to SL; no twist on the order-6 generator ρ
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the μ_4 inertia at j = 1728 (σ ↦ conjugate of σ^μ = σ^{χ_4(μ)})
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in GT action on B̂_3 (σ1σ2σ1 ↦ conjugate of its λ-th power) and in Nakamura's explicit formulae for Γ_{1,1}

ideas.what: Universal central involution ρ^3 = σ^2 in any quotient of SL(2,Z)^; transporting ξ and η to arbitrary finite quotients G (next page)
ideas.modern_name: centre of SL(2,Z) / Galois action on finite quotients (dessins of genus one, modular curves)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, correct computation in Grothendieck's own GT-style formalism of how the action lifts from PSL(2,Z)^ to SL(2,Z)^, including the χ_4 sign on σ. The content is equivalent to known facts about the GT/Galois action on B̂_3 and π̂_1(M_{1,1}) (Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps, Hain–Matsumoto). It is historically interesting as an early unpublished treatment, but not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The page number at bottom left is 526; the preceding page's footer reads 525, and the header '566' on the previous page is likely a misread.
In (17) the first line originally had a struck-over '+' sign ('ε = +1 ssi μ ≡ 1 (4)'). Under (16) the struck line reads 'ε = ε_2(μ)'.
The marginal note reads approximately: 'les soulignés désignent les éléments de GL(2,Ẑ) — et donc α̲ et β̲ en sont des images par …'. The remainder is illegible; it explains the underline convention.
In (16) the first line is likely u̲(ρ) = ξ̲ρ (or int(α̲)(ρ)). In the second line 'ε_?' is ε = ε_2(μ).
'SL(2,Z)^ est engendré topologiquement aussi par ρ et σ': 'topologiquement' is an interlinear addition.
In (18) the struck-out text is 'int ξ(β)' (written over), replaced by 'int(α̃)(ρ)'.
